Takeaways
Revenue
-- $789 million in the quarter, up five percent, marking a record for any fourth quarter in company history.
Operating ratio
-- 87.1 percent, deteriorated by 210 basis points from 85 percent due to new terminal startup costs, wage increases, and seasonal factors.
Earnings per diluted share
-- $2.84, down from $3.33.
Shipments per workday
-- Increased 4.5 percent in the quarter; December shipments up 7.2 percent, January up 6.5 percent.
Tonnage
-- Rose 10.1 percent in the quarter; December tonnage up 13.5 percent, January up 13.5 percent.
Weight per shipment
-- Increased 3.7 percent in the quarter, supporting revenue per shipment growth.
Length of haul
-- Up 0.3 percent to 898 miles.
Revenue per shipment ex-fuel surcharge
-- Up 1.3 percent to $299.17, representing a two percent sequential increase from Q3 2024.
Yield ex-fuel surcharge
-- Decreased 2.3 percent due to higher weight per shipment and ongoing mix optimization.
Yield (including fuel surcharge)
-- Declined 5.4 percent in the quarter.
Fuel surcharge revenue
-- 14.1 percent of revenue, down from 17 percent; decreased by 12.5 percent as diesel prices dropped over 17 percent year over year.
Contractual renewals
-- Averaged 7.9 percent in the quarter.
Number of terminals
-- 214 at year-end after opening 21 and relocating nine; company now has a national footprint.
Capital expenditures
-- Over $1 billion in 2024, mainly for real estate, equipment, and technology.
Depreciation expense
-- $54.1 million, up 18.3 percent due to asset additions.
Salaries, wages, and benefits expense
-- Rose 8.7 percent, reflecting 9.3 percent headcount growth and an average 4.1 percent wage increase.
Claims and insurance expense
-- Increased by 16.6 percent, attributed to "increased claims activity during the quarter, as well as unfavorable development of open cases."
Cost per shipment
-- Up 1.4 percent from last year’s quarter; flat for the full year at a 0.2 percent increase.
Purchase transportation expense
-- Down 11.1 percent, now 7.4 percent of revenue versus 8.7 percent last year.
Truck and rail PT miles
-- 13.1 percent of line-haul miles, down from about 15 percent a year ago.
Company cash and debt
-- Ended the year with just under $20 million cash and about $200 million total debt outstanding.
Full year revenue
-- $3.2 billion, a new record.
Full year operating income
-- $482.2 million.
Full year EPS
-- $13.51, up from $13.26.
New team members
-- Over 1,300 onboarded in 2024, reflecting significant network expansion.
On-time performance
-- "98 percent and above," comparable to industry peers.
Claims ratio
-- 0.59 percent for the quarter; 0.58 percent for the year.
Asset ownership
-- Over 9,900 doors with roughly 70 percent owned; 60 percent of terminals owned.
Capital expenditure guidance
-- Anticipates capex in excess of $700 million for 2025, with five to six facility additions planned.
Geographic exposure
-- Direct cross-border (Canada and Mexico) business about two percent of total revenue.

Risks
Operating ratio headwinds
-- Management stated, "these new openings in total remain a drag on the company OR," and full-year operating ratio deteriorated by 100 basis points to 85 percent.
Insurance costs
-- Claims and insurance expense rose 16.6 percent, driven by "increased claims activity during the quarter, as well as unfavorable development of open cases."
Quarterly margin pressure
-- Sequential margin deterioration is expected from Q4 to Q1, with Batteh indicating, "maybe we look at sort of a 30 to 50 basis points deterioration, from Q4 range."
Yield pressure
-- Decrease in yield ex-fuel surcharge (down 2.3 percent) attributed to heavier shipments, with no immediate normalization forecast by management.
Summary
Management emphasized record network expansion with 21 terminal openings, yielding shipment and tonnage growth, but at the expense of operating ratio and near-term profitability. Nearly three-quarters of volume gains in recent months were attributed to customers at newly opened terminals, which have yet to mature to company-average margins. The company remains focused on optimizing freight mix and pricing discipline, citing strong 7.9 percent contractual renewals and sequential improvements in revenue per shipment, while acknowledging transitory negative impacts from mix shifts and costs associated with ramping new capacity. Year-end cash and debt positions reflect over $1 billion in capital deployment, supported by a recently upsized revolving credit facility. Looking ahead, capital expenditure for 2025 is projected to exceed $700 million, targeting a modest number of new facilities as operational focus shifts toward maturing the national network and improving return on recent investments.
Management guided full-year operating ratio improvement of 80–100 basis points, with quarterly OR expected to improve sequentially after Q1 despite continued margin drag from new facilities.
January shipment and tonnage increases (6.5 percent and 13.5 percent, respectively) were heavily driven by 2024 terminal openings, indicating continued success in customer acquisition but ongoing below-average profitability at these sites.
Fuel surcharge revenue as a proportion of total revenue decreased to 14.1 percent, influenced by lower diesel costs and freight mix evolution.
Compensation expense, including a 4.1 percent wage hike and 9.3 percent workforce expansion, contributed to both volume growth and inflationary margin pressure as new employees integrate into expanded operations.
Claims ratio held below 0.6 percent, supporting competitive service quality even as claims and insurance expenses increased.
Management highlighted data-driven sales strategies and mix optimization as ongoing levers for future profitability and improved pricing power.
Industry glossary
Operating ratio (OR)
: A measure of operating expenses as a percentage of revenue, used to assess profitability in transportation/logistics firms; lower is better.
GRI (general rate increase)
: An across-the-board price increase implemented by carriers, usually on a contractual or annual basis.
Purchase transportation (PT)
: The use of third-party trucking or rail for line-haul or overflow capacity instead of company-owned fleet.
Yield
: Revenue per hundredweight or per shipment, indicating pricing effectiveness and freight mix.
Length of haul
: Average distance each shipment travels, used to analyze network usage and profitability.
Asset-light business
: Logistics services provided without direct ownership of transportation equipment or facilities.
Accessorial
: Additional charges for services outside standard freight (e.g., liftgate, inside delivery).
